archetypes.name: port-parity
archetypes.rationale: Checks whether the proposed Python changes actually mirror the bash rebase/re-bump contract without over- or under-scoping gates.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate whether the plan's has_bump and defer_push changes align with the existing rebase_and_rebump control flow and documented bash parity expectations. Look for missed side effects such as classify, apply, changelog commit, force-push, returned pushed state, or new_version handling that would make the written plan inconsistent with repo evidence. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: base-plumbing
archetypes.rationale: Targets contract drift around base_remote/base_ref propagation between rebase and version bump guards.
archetypes.prompt_body: Check whether the plan threads base_remote and base_ref through every proposed apply_bump guard site needed for the fork/upstream scenario while preserving documented default behavior. Verify that exclusions such as leaving classify_bump unchanged are supported by the stated scope and do not create an unacknowledged mismatch with the source issue. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: scope-boundary
archetypes.rationale: Looks for inconsistencies between the three-part reviewer description and the plan's intentional deferral of gap #1.
archetypes.prompt_body: Compare the reviewer description, scope file list, and implementation plan to ensure the deferred refresh-run-logs and larch-logs pre-drop fixup is handled as an explicit boundary rather than accidentally omitted. Look for wrong-target work, missing handoff notes, or file-scope contradictions caused by planning only gaps #2 and #3 from a combined issue. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
